predecessors.note: 'The dynasty began in 479, when Xiao Daocheng forced the Emperor Shun of Liu Song into yielding the throne'; infobox 'Established: 3 June 479' (the Liu Song ends 31 May 479). Cliopatria's Southern Qi shape is cell for cell the Liu Song shape of 451-479.

land.text: the Southern Qi shape of 500 without Shouyang, which Pei Shuye surrendered to the Wei in 500

successors.note: 'the last of which, by the general Xiao Yan led to Southern Qi's fall and succession by Xiao Yan's Liang Dynasty'; infobox 'Disestablished: 24 April 502' (the Liang page: 30 April 502).

capitals.name: Jiankang (Nanjing)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Jiankang'; the Wei raids led the Qi to 'fortify their capital, Jiankang'.

rulers.name: Xiao Zhaoye
rulers.note: Killed in the coup of 494; the Ming page dates the edict demoting him to 6 September 494.

rulers.name: Xiao Zhaowen
rulers.note: 'Less than three months' on the throne.

rulers.name: Ming (Xiao Luan)
rulers.note: Reign 5 December 494 - 1 September 498 (Emperor Ming page infobox).

rulers.name: Xiao Baojuan
rulers.note: Succeeded on Emperor Ming's death, 1 September 498 (Emperor Ming page infobox: reign '5 December 494 - 1 September 498', successor Xiao Baojuan; 'Crown Prince Baojuan succeeded him'); the table's Yongyuan era begins 499. Start year corrected from 499 by the ea-03-e reviewer so the ruler spans are contiguous.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 479: Cliopatria starts the Southern Qi in 480, but 'The dynasty began in 479' (infobox 3 June 479) and the Liu Song ended 31 May 479. The shape is the Southern Qi shape plus the Nanyang country (see southern-qi_480). The infobox gives no area (page silent).

keyframe_review.note: 2,361,556 km2 for 480-499, the same cells as the Liu Song shape of 451-479 (the infobox gives no area). It lacks the Nanyang country (8 of 50 cells within 60 km of Nanyang), which the Ming page has the Qi lose only in 497: 'the key border city Wancheng (in modern Nanyang, Henan) fell to Northern Wei' and 'as did Xinye'. Draw the corrected shape for 480-496 and this shape for 497-499 (southern-qi_497).

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape without Nanyang, valid from the fall of Wancheng and Xinye in 497

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 497-499, the Cliopatria shape unchanged: Wancheng and Xinye fell to the Wei in 497 (fall); the 495 campaign was abandoned in spring 495. Shouyang held until 500.

correction.text: the Southern Qi shape of 500 without Shouyang, which Pei Shuye surrendered to the Wei in 500

keyframe_review.note: 2,361,556 km2 for 500-509. Southern Qi ends 24 April 502, so 503-509 are the Liang's (new keyframes there). In 500 'Pei Shuye surrendered [Shouyang] to Northern Wei' (Emperor Wu of Liang page); Cliopatria keeps Shouyang (38 cells) in the Qi and Liang shapes until 509.

ledger.note: 479: the Wei prepare to invade and attack Shouyang. 'In 479, after Xiao Daocheng usurped the throne of Liu Song, the Northern Wei emperor prepared to invade'; 'Wei troops began to attack Shouyang but could not take the city' (undated).

union.text: Wancheng and Xinye, in modern Nanyang, Henan

region.text: the Southern Qi shape plus the Nanyang country (Wancheng, Xinye), Qi land until the Wei took it in 497

ledger.note: 479: Xiao Daocheng forces the last Liu Song emperor to yield the throne and founds the Southern Qi at Jiankang. 'The dynasty began in 479, when Xiao Daocheng forced the Emperor Shun of Liu Song into yielding the throne'; infobox 'Established: 3 June 479'.

481: the first Wei war dies away. 'Multiple sieges and skirmishes were fought until 481 but the war did not witness any major campaign.' The page adds a peace treaty 'signed in 490 with the Emperor Wu'.

region.text: Wancheng and Xinye, in modern Nanyang, Henan

ledger.note: 497: Wancheng and Xinye fall to the Wei. Northern Wei 'launched another major attack on Southern Qi' in 497: the key border city Wancheng (in modern Nanyang, Henan) 'fell to Northern Wei, as did Xinye'. Not in the northern-wei dossier.
500: Pei Shuye surrenders Shouyang to the Wei. The Wu of Liang page: 'Pei Shuye surrendered it to Northern Wei in 500'; the Liang retook it in summer 526.

region.text: the Southern Qi shape of 500 without Shouyang, which Pei Shuye surrendered to the Wei in 500

ledger.note: 502: Xiao Yan ends the Southern Qi and founds the Liang. Infobox 'Disestablished: 24 April 502'; 'the last of which, by the general Xiao Yan led to Southern Qi's fall and succession by Xiao Yan's Liang Dynasty'.

wars.name: Northern Wei-Southern Qi war of 479-481
wars.outcome: The Wei prepare an invasion in 479 and attack Shouyang without taking it; skirmishes continue to 481 with no major campaign.
wars.note: Peace treaty 'signed in 490 with the Emperor Wu' (the page's words; the Qi's Emperor Wu, Xiao Ze, reigned 482-493).

wars.name: Northern Wei invasions of 494-497

zones.text: Wancheng and Xinye, in modern Nanyang, Henan

wars.outcome: A major Wei attack in late 494 is abandoned in spring 495; another in 497 takes Wancheng and Xinye (Nanyang).

wars.name: Wang Jingze's rebellion
wars.outcome: A retired general rebels in summer 498 and is killed in battle about twenty days later; no territory.
wars.note: An internal revolt, listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; it held no land.

wars.name: Xiao Yan's march on Jiankang
wars.outcome: Pei Shuye surrenders Shouyang to the Wei in 500; Xiao Yan ends the Southern Qi in April 502.

certainty.note: No treaty line survives on the pages: the peace of 490 is named without a frontier. The Huai and Han frontiers are approximate.

sources.title: Southern Qi
sources.note: Identity, dates (3 June 479 - 24 April 502), capital, emperors, the 479-481 Wei war, the 490 peace. The infobox gives no area; silent on Jiaozhou, Champa and the Hanzhong and Huaibei lands.

sources.title: Emperor Ming of Southern Qi
sources.note: Wei invasions of 494-497, Wancheng and Xinye in 497, Wang Jingze's rebellion in 498, emperors' dates.

sources.title: Emperor Wu of Liang
sources.note: Pei Shuye's surrender of Shouyang in 500 (a third page, over the budget of two, for the only dated territorial loss under Qi besides Nanyang).

notes: Cliopatria row 'Southern Qi' 480-509 has two identical 2,361,556 km2 shapes that are cell for cell the Liu Song shapes of 451-479, and runs seven years past the 502 end (503-509 are the Liang's). The infobox gives no area. Corrections: the Nanyang country is Qi land until 497 (the Cliopatria shape lacks it), Shouyang goes in 500. NOT SETTLED: (1) the pages opened are silent on Jiaozhou, Champa, Hanzhong and Yongzhou, so the south and the west stand unverified; (2) the 490 peace and whether it fixed a frontier; (3) the Wei war of 495-499 beyond the fall of Wancheng and Xinye in 497 (the Ming page is silent on 498 and 499); (4) Xinye and Wancheng are read as a 60 km disc round Nanyang; (5) the northern-wei dossier has no 497 gain from the Qi, nor a 500 gain of Shouyang: both are for that dossier's gap-filler. Page budget: two pages, plus the Emperor Wu of Liang page opened for liang-dynasty.
